paragraphs: Rabbi Tanchum son of Mari; Ketubot 8:10.

notes.text: The frozen text reads רבה מר מרי. Berakhot42b in the William Davidson edition has Rabbah bar Mari; bar is bracketed as the proposed reading rather than silently changing the Hebrew.

Hyman’s printed page (vol. III, p. 903) reads “Rabbah Mar Mari.” Berakhot 42b has Rabbah bar Mari both in the discussion of blessings over wine and in the account of his visit to Rava. The Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubot 8:10, names Rabbi Tanchum bar Mari reporting Rabbi Yose in the discussion of property subject to a lien. These references do not establish that the two men had the same father.
